rv.q: That’s not only the case with Pride , it’s also central to the story of this glorious, heartbreaking musical and its galvanising message of hope.
The rest of the original music, variously credited to Josh Cohen, DJ Walde and Christopher Nightingale, is efficient rather than inspirational.
Funny, moving, uplifting and profoundly relevant, Pride the Musical is a testament to the courage of those who refuse to accept injustice and the communities which find strength in standing together.
It isn't perfect, but it's the perfect story for a musical, perfectly told.
Fuelled by hope, solidarity and their love of a laugh, the two communities transform division into unity through an extraordinary bond of friendship.
This is ensemble theatremaking at its most endearing, combining social and political grit with unashamed flamboyance.
It’s great news for theatre-goers that Pride’s transfer to a larger space for a longer run means that so many people will get to experience this outstanding production.
All in all, Pride: The Musical is a success for its ability to provide a great night out while exposing a powerful story.
This is the early favourite to win next year's Olivier for Best Musical and, in the words of 1 of its bangers, a Bloody Good Night Out .
The stage adaptation remains remarkably faithful to the heart, humour, and emotional beats of the movie.
It is actually an endearing piece. And for the most part, it's quite entertaining. But it isn't brilliant, by any means.

cn.t: Pride the Musical earns near-universal acclaim as a joyful, heartfelt celebration of LGBTQ+ and miners' solidarity. Most critics hail it as essential, crowd-pleasing theatre, with a lone dissenter calling it "cosy politics."
